correctness.rationale: The all-k proof reconstructs cleanly. If M+i with 1<=i<=k-1 were k-smooth, truncating each exponent at r_p gives a common divisor of M and M+i that contains q^{r_q}>k for some exceeded exponent, hence is larger than i while dividing i, a contradiction. For each p<=k, writing M=p^rQ shows that M-1 has p-1 in its lowest r base-p positions. Adding k first carries at t=nu_p(k), propagates through positions t,...,r-1, and stops at r because p does not divide Q. Kummer therefore gives nu_p(C(M+k-1,k))=r_p-nu_p(k)>=1. The finite k<=120 verifier is corroborative only.
